items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: I was nominated along with Chucho Valdes, Miguel Zenon, Claudio Roditi, and Geoff Keezer

ctx.x: So what’s it like to make a living as a musician in New York City. Do you have to wear lots of hats?

Oh yeah, especially for myself, I’m an independent record company, Chemboro Records, I’ve had it since 2004. I have five CDs under my label. The third CD, “Things I Wanted to Do” in 2010 was nominated for a Grammy of Best Latin Jazz by the American Grammy, NARAS. I was nominated along with Chucho Valdes, Miguel Zenon, Claudio Roditi, and Geoff Keezer, pianist I guess. But when you have a name like Chucho Valdes, “Who is Chembo?” “Who is Chembo?” But at least being nominated and being an independent, so I have to…

to the music. They say, “La clave es la llave.” The clave is the key. Okay? So the reason why is that when you play clave, which is say a three-two, I’m going to tap it like [claps] right? Everybody knows that. This is a two bar phrase. One-two-three-four, one-two- three-four, one-two-three-four, two-two-three four. Right on two-three-four, two. So this is a two bar phrase. In that music we write in two bar phrases so you won’t jump. In jazz you do one bar, one bar here and there, and that’s why you know you…
